1: Writing from prison, Paul thanks God for the Philippians and is sure that God, who began a good work in them, will finish it. His chains have helped spread the Gospel. He is torn between dying to be with Christ and staying to serve them.
Paul's joy does not depend on his circumstances. "To live is Christ, and to die is gain."
2: Paul asks for unity and humility, each looking to the interests of others. He quotes a hymn: Christ, though in the form of God, emptied himself, became a servant and was obedient to death on a cross. So God exalted him, and every knee shall bow.
This is one of the earliest statements that Jesus is God. His way down is the model for how Christians treat one another.
3: Paul lists his impressive Jewish credentials and calls them rubbish compared with knowing Christ. He has not arrived yet; he presses on toward the goal. "Our citizenship is in heaven."
Knowing Jesus outweighs every achievement. The Christian life is a race still being run.
4: Paul urges two women to be reconciled. Do not be anxious; bring everything to God in prayer with thanksgiving, and his peace will guard your hearts. Think about whatever is true and honourable. Paul has learned to be content in any situation.
Paul writes this from prison. "I can do all things through him who strengthens me."
